content.text:
For today’s investor pitch, I can help you get to a crisp deck + narrative fast. Here’s a tight structure you can follow (and I can draft slides if you share bullets/metrics):

## Pitch backbone (10–12 slides)
1) **One-liner**: CloudScale simplifies cloud deployments for ___ by ___.
2) **Problem**: what’s broken today (cost/complexity/time-to-deploy/risk).
3) **Solution**: what you do differently (architecture + UX) in 3 bullets.
4) **Why now**: market shift (serverless adoption, platform engineering, cost pressure).
5) **Product**: quick demo flow or screenshot sequence (before/after).
6) **Traction**: revenue, growth, retention, usage, logos, pipeline (pick 3–5).
7) **Project Phoenix**: serverless platform—why it matters, timeline to beta/Q2 launch, expected impact.
8) **Moat**: tech differentiation, data/learning, integrations, switching costs, team.
9) **Go-to-market**: who buys, sales motion, ACV, sales cycle, channels.
10) **Financials**: ARR, gross margin, burn, runway, LTV/CAC (or what you have).
11) **Series C ask**: amount, use of funds (hiring plan), milestones to hit.
12) **Team**: why you/Sarah/Dave can win.

- Target **Series C amount** and runway goal
- Top **3 traction metrics** you want to feature (even rough)
- Ideal **ICP** (who buys) + typical deal size/sales cycle
- 2–3 key **Phoenix differentiators** (latency, cost, DX, security, etc.)
